run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T01:33:10Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by transport-level failures on exactly two call paths: frontend→ad (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, 390 failing spans in the 30m ending 01:45) and checkout→payment surfaced through frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder ('13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused', 43 spans). The dialled addresses are the ClusterIPs of Service ad (100.65.180.246) and Service payment (100.70.188.60), not pod IPs (pods are 100.96.x). Frontend error spans started between 01:32:00 and 01:33:00 and stopped after 01:40:00, and the ad and payment server-side span rates were exactly zero in that window: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds rate was 0 at every minute from 01:34:00 to 01:41:00 (before: ~0.4–0.68/s, after: ~0.8/s at 01:42:00), payment's charge rate 0 at 01:34:00 and 01:35:00 (resumed 01:36:00). Both Deployments ad and payment were rolled at 2026-11-17T01:31:36Z (new ReplicaSets annotated kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, template otherwise identical, old pods killed 01:31:39/01:31:40, new containers started 01:31:38/39, no readiness/liveness/startup probes, restartCount 0). The supported picture is that the freshly started ad (and payment) containers were not accepting connections for several minutes after the rollout while their Services kept sending traffic to them, so callers got TCP connection refused. The fault-injection flags currently present in ConfigMap flagd-config (adFailure=on, paymentFailure=100%) are reported as a candidate, not as the cause: their declared behaviour would produce application-level failures with ad/payment server spans, whereas ad and payment recorded zero server spans in the failure window. The trigger of the 01:31:36 rollout restart and the reason the apps took minutes to listen are unresolved (no change history, no frontend/flagd logs).

claims.text: Frontend error spans rose from a cumulative 2126 at 01:32:00 to 3833 at 01:40:00 and stayed flat afterwards; frontend-proxy error spans rose from 1074 to 1941 in the same interval, and checkout error spans rose 18→84 between 01:33:00 and 01:34:00 (all values: cumulative error-span counters of traces_span_metrics_calls_total).

In the 30 minutes ending 01:45:00 the frontend error spans were concentrated on GET/api/data (390 error spans) and its grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds child (390), plus the checkout path POST/api/checkout (43) and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (43); frontend-proxy recorded errors on span 'ingress' (454.86) and 'router frontend egress' (433.35) in the same window.

The exact diagnostics on the failing frontend spans are: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds → rpc.grpc.status_code=14, rpc error message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder → rpc.grpc.status_code=13, '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

100.65.180.246 is the ClusterIP of Service ad and 100.70.188.60 is the ClusterIP of Service payment (ports 8080→targetPort 8080, selectors opentelemetry.io/name=ad and =payment); the corresponding pods have different addresses (ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 = 100.96.4.142, payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 = 100.96.4.221), so the refused connections were addressed to the Services, not to the pods.

Deployments ad and payment were both rolled at the same instant: ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 were created 2026-11-17T01:31:36Z with the template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:31:36Z, while the previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 were scaled to 0 replicas; image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad / 2.1.3-payment), env, ports and resources are identical between old and new templates.

Events in namespace otel-demo show the rollout sequence: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Scheduled 01:31:36, image already present and container Started 01:31:38, old pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm 'Killing/Stopping container ad' 01:31:39; payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 container Started 01:31:39, old pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb 'Killing/Stopping container payment' 01:31:40; Deployment ad/payment 'ScalingReplicaSet' events up then down.

The new ad and payment pods have no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe; their containers are running since 01:31:38Z / 01:31:39Z with ready=true, restartCount=0 and empty lastState (no OOMKilled or crash), and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff event exists for them in otel-demo in the window.

ad and payment served no requests during the caller failure window: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) was ~0.41–0.68/s up to 01:33:00, exactly 0 at every evaluation from 01:34:00 through 01:41:00, and resumed at 0.80/s at 01:42:00; payment's 'charge' span rate was ~0.26–0.47/s before, 0 at 01:34:00 and 01:35:00, and resumed 0.62/s at 01:36:00.

The new ad container's earliest stdout line inside 01:25:00–01:49:15 is 01:39:32 (276 lines total, all between 01:39:32 and 01:41:02, no previous container instance), and the new payment container's earliest line is 01:38:16 (593 lines, 01:38:16–01:41:05), i.e. neither container logged anything from its 01:31:38/39 start until those times.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo currently declares fault-injection flags with 'adFailure' defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Fail ad service') and 'paymentFailure' defaultVariant '100%' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'); all other flags (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) are 'off'.

In the 30 minutes ending 01:45:00 no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were recorded for product-catalog (GetProduct/ListProducts), cart's CartService/GetCart and /AddItem, currency (Currency/Convert), shipping, quote, email, or recommendation's ListRecommendations — frontend's and checkout's calls to those dependencies show only non-error spans, so the failing paths are limited to ad (GetAds) and payment (charge/PlaceOrder).

At query time the Services ad and payment have populated endpoints pointing at the new pods (ad → 100.96.4.142 / ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6; payment → 100.96.4.221 / payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84), i.e. the endpoint mapping is correct now; this is the cluster's state at query time and does not show the incident window.

Primary causal chain: the 01:31:36 rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment replaced the serving pods with containers that started at 01:31:38/39 but did not accept gRPC connections for several minutes (ad ~01:39–01:41, payment ~01:36); since neither Deployment defines a readiness probe, the Services kept routing to the new pods, so frontend's GetAds calls and checkout's Charge calls were rejected at the ClusterIPs (ECONNREFUSED) until the apps began listening. This is consistent with zero ad/payment server spans during the failure window and with the errors stopping when those spans resumed, but the reason the apps took minutes to listen is not established.

Candidate kept open: the fault-injection flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (adFailure=on, paymentFailure=100%) are named for the two failing call paths, so they cannot be dismissed outright. However their declared behaviour is an application-level failure of ad/payment, whereas the observed failure is a TCP connection refusal to the Service ClusterIPs with ad and payment recording zero server spans in the window; the flag values must also be treated as the ConfigMap's state at query time, not as its value during 01:31–01:40.

Second candidate: a slow or failing startup dependency (both ad and payment use FLAGD_HOST=flagd/FLAGD_PORT=8013, and ad's error spans include flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) may explain why the restarted containers produced no logs and served no requests for minutes. No flagd-side metric series or flagd container log lines were returned, so this remains unverified.

The flagd-config fault flags are not producing failures at query time: frontend's cumulative error-span counter is flat at 3833 at 01:44:00, 01:45:00, 01:46:00 and 01:47:00 (rate 0) while adFailure is still 'on' and paymentFailure still '100%', and ad's GetAds span rate was back at 0.80/s by 01:42:00 — so these flag values alone do not currently generate the observed errors.

Rejected: a defect inside frontend itself. The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 has been running since 00:57:53Z with restartCount 0 and was not rolled during the window, its failing spans are gRPC transport failures addressed to the ad and payment Service ClusterIPs, and its calls to product-catalog, cart, currency, shipping, quote, email and recommendation recorded no error spans.

Rejected: ad/payment pods crashed, were OOMKilled or Evicted. Their containers have been running continuously since 01:31:38Z/01:31:39Z with restartCount 0, empty lastState and ready=true, and no OOMKilled, Evicted or BackOff event exists for them in the namespace events; the pods are Ready, which is why readiness cannot be used here to detect that the application socket was not yet open.

Add a readinessProbe (and gRPC health check) to the ad and payment containers so their Services stop sending traffic to a pod whose server socket is not yet listening, and review why the restarted ad/payment containers needed minutes before serving (startup dependency on flagd) — verification of the trigger is advisory work for a human, not performed here.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what issued the kubectl-style rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:31:36Z) on Deployments ad and payment, and whether ConfigMap flagd-config was edited at that time, cannot be verified.
ConfigMap flagd-config was read only at query time; its value during 01:31–01:40, and whether flagd reloaded it, are unknown (the ConfigMap has no revision history in the evidence).
The frontend container returned no stdout lines at all for 01:28–01:45 (query returned no data), so there are no application log lines to corroborate the trace error details from the frontend side.

The flagd pod's container logs returned no lines for 01:20–01:45 and no traces_span_metrics_calls_total series exist for service_name=flagd, so flagd's own health and flag delivery during the incident are unknown.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no series for namespace otel-demo (query returned nothing), so the readiness/availability of the ad and payment Deployments over time could not be charted.

A NetworkPolicy query across all namespaces returned nothing (status no_data), so the absence of network policies cannot be asserted; network-level causes other than the observed refusals remain unverified.

Jaeger's latest trace data for this target was as of ~01:32:44, so error-detail inspection of the later part of the error window (01:34–01:40) was not possible; the error text is documented for the 01:32:39–01:32:44 slice only.

Prometheus alerting rules could not be listed (rule_name RequestErrorRate and type=alert both returned no data), so the exact PromQL and the reported 'current: 2.5777' value of the alert could not be verified.

Some metric views changed shape between queries (e.g. a rate(1m) evaluation returned zeros and skipped minutes where cumulative counters showed increases); the timelines reported above are the ones consistently reproduced by the cumulative-counter and rate(2m) queries, and the discrepancy itself is unexplained.
next_steps: Check cluster audit logs / change management for the identity and method behind the 2026-11-17T01:31:36Z rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment and any flagd-config edit at that time.

Inspect ad and payment startup behaviour after the restart (image entrypoint waits, flagd subscription on boot) to explain the multi-minute gap between container start 01:31:38/39 and first served request (~01:36 payment, ~01:41 ad).

Verify that flagd is delivering demo.flagd.json to ad and payment, and decide whether the currently set adFailure=on / paymentFailure=100% values are intended, since they do not match the observed failure mechanism.
Confirm downstream/customer impact (e.g. failed checkouts and HTTP 500 rate at the ingress during 01:33–01:40) before reporting customer-visible impact, which was not directly measured here.
